thought.text: Probe client removed. Now let me create a test user with both roles assigned, and check the npm install progress.

reasoning_content: The problem was a race condition: the shell was reusing an old token file. With a new token, it worked. probe2 has already been deleted. Next, I'll create a test user "user1" with the app-access + editor roles assigned, then check the npm installation status.

action.command: TOK=$(cat /tmp/kc-token.txt) && curl -s -X POST "http://localhost:8080/admin/realms/my-realm/users" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOK" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"username":"user1","firstName":"Test","lastName":"User","email":"user1@example.com","enabled":true,"emailVerified":true}' -w "create user: HTTP:%{http_code}\n" && UID1=$(curl -s "http://localhost:8080/admin/realms/my-realm/users?username=user1" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOK" | jq -r '.[0].id') && echo "user1 id: $UID1" && for role in app-access editor; do curl -s -X PUT "http://localhost:8080/admin/realms/my-realm/users/$UID1/role-mappings/clients/$(cat /tmp/client_id.txt)/$role" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOK" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '[{"name":"'$role'","composite":false,"clientRole":true,"containerId":"'"$(cat /tmp/client_id.txt)"'"}]' -w "assign $role: HTTP:%{http_code}\n"; done
